messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen@cobaltai.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Lightweight tracing + prompt-toolkit integration with Redwood

Hi Sofia,

Quick intro — I’m Ellen (Head of Platform Partnerships) at CobaltAI. We build a small, highly composable prompt toolkit and an ISV SDK that many LangChain / LlamaIndex users embed. Marco from PromptWorks suggested we reach out to align on a lightweight tracing and prompt-metadata integration so customers can see model spans, prompt versions, and tool calls in Redwood Console.

We’re hoping to: 
- Ship a tiny adapter that emits Redwood-compatible tracing headers and a compact prompt hash,
- Add optional instrumented helpers for prefix caching hints and model-variant annotations, and
- Include a short example for LangChain and LlamaIndex adapter usage.

Before we jump to an engineering sync, could you share: 
1) high-level onboarding steps 
2) any acceptance criteria you require for ISV SDKs (tests, signal surface) 
3) an example trace payload/headers you expect 

I can loop in our lead engineer (Marco Liu) and we can push a small repo + patch. We’re targeting a minimal first-integration in ~2 weeks if that cadence works.

Thanks — really excited to get this working with Redwood.

Best,
Ellen Park
Head of Platform Partnerships, CobaltAI
ellen@cobaltai.com
+1 415-555-0123

Attachments: none (I’ll share a sample repo link in a follow-up)
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen@cobaltai.com>
Cc: Marco Liu <marco@promptworks.io>
Date: 2028-05-20T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Lightweight tracing + prompt-toolkit integration with Redwood

Hi Ellen — thanks for the clear note and intro. This is exactly the sort of small, composable integration we want to support. Happy to run a short call to align on scope. I’m copying our partner lead (Vanessa) and runtime engineer (Karthik) so we have the right folks on the thread.

High-level onboarding steps (what we’ll expect from the ISV):
- Quick scoping call (30m) to confirm surface area and a target customer/workflow
- Small sample repo or patch (public or private) that shows how you emit traces and prompt metadata
- Sanity tests: one end-to-end trace emitted for a LangChain call and one for a LlamaIndex flow
- Lightweight docs: README + minimal telemetry field descriptions
- Optional: small compatibility shim for our SDK (we can provide a template)

Minimum acceptance criteria (our side):
- Traces include a stable trace_id and span_id(s) so we can join spans in Console
- Model span contains model_variant, token_count, and latency_ms
- Prompt metadata includes a prompt_hash and prompt_version (helps regression tracking)
- Instrumentation optional flag so customers can opt into emissions

Example trace headers we typically accept (simple HTTP header form):
- X-Redwood-Trace-Id: <uuid>
- X-Redwood-Span-Id: <hex>
- X-Redwood-Model: model-name@variant
- X-Redwood-Prompt-Hash: <sha1>

If you can share the sample repo link I’ll ask Karthik to sketch the runtime checklist and Vanessa will pick the partner owner and next steps. Proposed slot for a sync: Mon 2028-05-22 10:30am PT — does that work?

Regards,
Sofia Ivanova
Head of Partner Integrations, Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.com

Forwarding Ellen’s request — short summary below and suggested acceptance checklist. Can one of you take ownership?

Summary: CobaltAI (with PromptWorks helping) wants to emit Redwood-friendly traces from an ISV SDK used by LangChain/LlamaIndex integrations. They’ll provide a sample repo and want a short onboarding window (~2 weeks).

Suggested technical acceptance checklist (runtime):
- End-to-end sample: a single LangChain prompt -> model -> tool flow that produces: 
  * trace_id, span_id, model_variant, token_count, latency_ms
  * prompt_hash and prompt_version in model-span metadata
- Backward compatibility: instrumentation must be opt-in via an env var or explicit client flag
- Prefetch/prefix caching hint: optional header (X-Redwood-Cache-Hint) to mark cacheable prompt prefixes
- CI smoke test: a minimal test that validates a trace appears in our sandbox Console (we’ll provide a sandbox token)
- Security review: no PII leakage in telemetry fields; add a short privacy checklist in README

Attachments: redwood_onboarding-checklist.pdf (I attached our lightweight template) and I can draft a starter adapter for them. ETA request: can we commit to review/smoke within 3 business days of receiving the sample repo?

Thanks — looped Vanessa for partner coordination and Karthik for runtime details.

— Sofia

Thanks all — quick status update and a minimal sample to unblock the review. Marco pushed a tiny repo (link below) and attached a patch with the header mapping we propose: 

Sample header payload (HTTP):

  "X-Redwood-Trace-Id": "4b8f9a2e-1f3c-4a6b-a7d3-2a9f7b1c0e6d",
  "X-Redwood-Span-Id": "1a2b3c4d5e",
  "X-Redwood-Model": "open-mosaic@v1.2-q4_0",
  "X-Redwood-Prompt-Hash": "sha1:9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b",
  "X-Redwood-Cache-Hint": "prefix=customer_profile;ttl=120"
}

We also added a tiny code snippet (in the repo) that instruments a LangChain LLM wrapper and emits the headers on the model call. Example snippet from the repo:

We attached: trace-integration-snippet.patch (small changes to the SDK) and uploaded the sample repo to: https://github.com/cobaltai/prompt-kit-sample (private until approval).
